strategy.summary: Reproduce pandas numerical correctness bugfix for GH#43178 as extended by PR#65515: overflow-safe multiplication/division for timedelta64[ns] scalars/arrays should raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta instead of silently wrapping/saturating. The reproducing check is pandas’ own new tests in pandas/tests/arithmetic/test_timedelta64.py; they must fail on buggy pandas revision 4a704a111961 and pass on the fixed revision.

build_commands: python -m pip install -U pip setuptools wheel
pip install Cython==<choose version compatible with your toolchain>
pip install numpy==1.21.2 python-dateutil==2.8.2 pytz==2021.1 pytest
pinned_because: NumPy is explicitly constrained to 1.21.2 (documented, numerically relevant) from issue#43178.
python-dateutil and pytz are explicitly constrained (documented) from issue#43178; while not numerically relevant, keep them fixed for environment determinism.
Cython/pytest versions are not documented/constraint-pinned in the provided evidence; select compatible versions for your platform rather than assuming a specific one.

strategy.test_command: python -m pytest pandas/tests/arithmetic/test_timedelta64.py -k "td64arr_mul_int_overflow or td64arr_mul_uint_overflow or td64arr_mul_int_min_boundary or td64arr_mul_float_overflow or td64arr_mul_float_overflow_boundary or td64arr_mul_inf_raises"
strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/arithmetic/test_timedelta64.py::TestTimedelta64ArrayArithmetic (new tests added by PR#65515): test_td64arr_mul_int_overflow, test_td64arr_mul_uint_overflow, test_td64arr_mul_int_min_boundary, test_td64arr_mul_float_overflow, test_td64arr_mul_float_overflow_boundary, test_td64arr_mul_inf_raises
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision (git checkout 4a704a111961), the relevant pytest assertions that expect OutOfBoundsTimedelta to be raised will FAIL (i.e., no OutOfBoundsTimedelta is raised, or the raised exception/message does not match the expected regex). On the fixed revision (the commit that includes PR#65515’s fix), the same tests will PASS by raising OutOfBoundsTimedelta with message matching the regex strings used in the tests: "Overflow in int64 multiplication" and "Overflow in timedelta multiplication"/"Overflow in timedelta division".
strategy.numerical_probe: Trigger overflow paths in pandas._libs.tslibs.np_datetime.mul_overflowsafe via TimedeltaIndex multiplication/division on timedelta64[ns]. The tests explicitly use boundaries that historically caused silent int64 wrap or float->int cast saturation instead of overflow-safe raising.

input_output_examples.input: td = pd.Timedelta(100000, "D").as_unit("ns"); x = pd.Series([td, td]); x * 2
td = pd.Timedelta(100000, "D").as_unit("ns"); x = pd.Series([td, td]); x / 0.4

risks: This strategy targets only the multiplication/division overflow-safe raising behaviour exercised by the PR#65515 tests listed in test_command. If the buggy revision 4a704a111961 does not reproduce the raising-based behaviour on your platform/toolchain, you may need to broaden to other overflow tests in the same file (e.g., cumsum/other sum precision-loss issues), but that would no longer match the provided failing diff precisely.

The evidence does not provide the fixed commit SHA. You must identify the fixed revision (e.g., by checking out the pandas commit after PR#65515 is merged or the PR’s merge commit) and run the same test_command to confirm the PASS transition.

Cython and pytest versions are not pinned by evidence; while they typically won’t change runtime overflow logic, mismatched build environments can affect extension compilation and thus whether the overflow-safe code path is exercised.

Potential architecture/platform dependency: if the overflow-safe logic is implemented differently for certain builds (32-bit vs 64-bit, or specific SIMD/CPU settings), the failure may not transition. Run on the same architecture as the original bug report when possible (most CI is x86_64 Linux).

The provided examples mention silent wrapping/saturation and other sum precision failures, but the reproducing test chosen here is the one added/modified in the provided diff; the success criterion is based strictly on exceptions being raised with matching messages, not on numerical values being printed.

oracle.reference_source: pandas/tests/arithmetic/test_timedelta64.py (expected OutOfBoundsTimedelta with match regexes defined in the tests).
oracle.why: The diff’s tests use pytest.raises(OutOfBoundsTimedelta, match=msg) so correctness is determined by exception type + message regex match, which is an exact/oracle-style check (not a numeric tolerance check).

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The new overflow tests will fail because buggy code does not raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta on overflow (previously it silently wrapped/saturated, or raised a different exception / different message). Therefore pytest.raises(OutOfBoundsTimedelta, match=...) will not be satisfied for at least one of the selected tests (likely test_td64arr_mul_int_overflow or test_td64arr_mul_float_overflow).
strategy.passes_on_fixed: After checking out the pandas fixed revision (the one that includes PR#65515’s overflow-safe changes to pandas._libs.tslibs.np_datetime.mul_overflowsafe / overflow detection), the same tests raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta with the expected messages, so pytest assertions pass.
